Name: Backend for Frontend (BFF)
Pattern: Dedicated backend service per frontend platform (iOS/Android/Web)
Use Case: Optimize API responses per platform — different payloads for mobile vs web
Strengths: Tailored responses reduce over-fetching; independent deployment per platform; cleaner API contracts
Weaknesses: Duplicated business logic across BFFs; more services to maintain; team coordination overhead
Gotcha: BFF should be thin — only aggregation and transformation; business logic stays in domain services

Name: Offline-First Sync
Pattern: Local-first data with background sync to server when connectivity restored
Use Case: Mobile apps that must work without network — field service and travel and rural areas
Strengths: Works offline; responsive UX; conflict detection built in
Weaknesses: Conflict resolution is complex; storage limits on device; sync bugs are hard to reproduce
Gotcha: Last-write-wins loses data — use vector clocks or CRDTs for automatic conflict resolution; test with airplane mode

Name: Push Notification Delivery
Use Case: Real-time alerts and messages and updates to mobile devices
Strengths: Instant delivery; battery efficient (vs polling); platform-native UX
Weaknesses: Platform-specific APIs; delivery not guaranteed; token management complexity
Gotcha: APNs tokens expire and rotate — implement token refresh and feedback service processing or notifications silently fail

Name: GraphQL for Mobile
Pattern: Single flexible endpoint with client-specified queries
Use Case: Mobile clients that need different data shapes per screen with minimal over-fetching
Strengths: Eliminates over-fetching; single round trip for complex views; strong typing
Weaknesses: Query complexity attacks; N+1 at resolver level; caching harder than REST; learning curve
Gotcha: Always implement query depth and complexity limits — unbounded GraphQL queries can DoS your backend

Name: CDN for API Responses
Pattern: Cache API responses at CDN edge for read-heavy mobile endpoints
Use Case: Static or semi-static API responses — product catalogs and config and feature flags
Strengths: Dramatically reduces latency and origin load; global distribution; cost effective
Weaknesses: Cache invalidation complexity; personalized responses can't be cached easily; stale data risk
Gotcha: Set appropriate Cache-Control headers — mobile apps aggressively cache so stale CDN + stale app cache compounds staleness

Name: API Versioning for Mobile
Pattern: Version APIs to support old app versions that can't be force-updated
Use Case: Mobile apps where users don't update — must support v1 and v2 simultaneously
Strengths: Backward compatibility; graceful deprecation; per-version monitoring
Weaknesses: Maintaining multiple versions is expensive; version sprawl; database schema must serve all versions
Gotcha: iOS App Store review takes 1-7 days — you can't hotfix mobile apps like web; API versioning is your safety net

Name: Optimistic UI Updates
Pattern: Apply changes locally immediately then confirm/revert after server response
Use Case: Perceived-zero-latency interactions — likes and toggles and form submissions
Strengths: Instant feedback; feels native; reduces perceived latency to zero
Weaknesses: Must handle server rejection gracefully; complex rollback UI; conflict with server state
Gotcha: If optimistic update succeeds locally but fails on server the user sees a jarring revert — show clear feedback and retry option

Name: Token Refresh Flow
Pattern: Background refresh of auth tokens before expiration to avoid re-login
Use Case: Seamless authentication in mobile apps without interrupting user flow
Strengths: No re-login interruption; secure short-lived access tokens; background refresh
Weaknesses: Race conditions with concurrent requests during refresh; token storage security on device
Gotcha: Implement request queuing during token refresh — concurrent 401s should wait for refresh not each trigger their own

Name: Image Optimization Pipeline
Pattern: Server-side image resizing and format conversion and CDN caching per device
Use Case: Serve appropriately-sized images per device — reduce bandwidth and improve load time
Strengths: Reduces bandwidth 50-80%; improves Core Web Vitals; automatic format selection (WebP/AVIF)
Weaknesses: Processing cost for on-the-fly resizing; cache storage for multiple variants; origin shield needed
Gotcha: Serve WebP to Android and AVIF to modern iOS — Accept header detection at CDN level; don't send 4K images to phones

Name: App Startup Optimization
Pattern: Minimize time-to-interactive with prefetching and lazy loading and cached bootstrap data
Use Case: Fast app launch — first screen content appears in under 1 second
Strengths: Better retention (1s faster = measurable engagement increase); reduced abandonment
Weaknesses: Over-prefetching wastes bandwidth; cache invalidation bugs show stale launch data
Gotcha: Cache the minimal bootstrap response locally — if the server is slow the app still opens fast with last-known-good data
